teaser.text: Johnson & Johnson is a healthcare company that sells prescription medicines and medical devices. Its dollar comes in when a product reaches a paying customer, and goes out through research, manufacturing, distribution, people, partners, and investment.

blocks.heading: Where could Johnson & Johnson's shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: The forecast points to a near-term decline before a modest recovery. The weighted price is $229.07 in October 2027, a 6% loss with dividends. It rises to $239.91 in October 2028, a 1% gain. By October 2029, it reaches $251.90, an 8% gain.

The central case has 53% probability. The bear case has 27%, while the bull case has 20%. The October 2029 range runs from $143.33 in the bear case to $384.60 in the bull case. Today's price is $248.61, so the forecast sees moderate expected returns but substantial execution risk.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Johnson & Johnson—and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The bear case holds earnings near $26,520 million in the first year and then allows only slight improvement, as replacement sales lag, biosimilars pressure margins and separation costs persist. TREMFYA replaced only about 35% of STELARA's 2025 revenue decline, while Q3 MedTech growth was 2.5%. The bull case reaches $36,500 million by 2029, requiring faster TREMFYA, oncology and neuroscience growth plus expanding margins. J&J's $55 billion investment programme supports that possibility, but does not make it the central outcome.

The bear case assumes biosimilar erosion outpaces replacement, MedTech stays uneven and separation costs pressure margins. Talc payments then limit buybacks, while weaker earnings durability compresses the P/E. The price falls to $175.77 in October 2027 and $143.33 by October 2029. Its 27% probability reflects the combined downside assigned to earnings and valuation, while dividends and shares provide only limited protection.

blocks.heading: How much does Johnson & Johnson pay per share?

paragraphs.text: Dividends rise from $5.44 per share to $5.77 in the base case, near the latest 3.1% increase. The bear case holds $5.36 throughout, a pause rather than a cut. The bull case reaches $5.92 because stronger cash generation permits faster increases. J&J's 64-year record of consecutive increases and 2026 free-cash-flow guidance support continued growth, but talc payments and debt limit confidence.

blocks.heading: Is Johnson & Johnson's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: Profit records accounting income; cash flow records money collected and paid. J&J’s operating cash flow was $24,530 million in 2025, while free cash flow after capital spending was $19,536 million. A sale may be recorded before the customer pays, and inventory may consume cash before it is sold.

Dividends distribute cash to owners, while buybacks purchase shares and can increase each remaining share’s claim on future earnings. J&J’s large shareholder payments left little annual surplus for acquisitions. That matters because acquisitions still required substantial cash, while sales of businesses and assets supplied much less.

blocks.heading: What is Johnson & Johnson's dividend yield against its price?

paragraphs.text: At $248.61, shareholders value J&J’s equity at $599,125 million. Enterprise value is $627,403 million because it adds net debt to the equity value. The difference is like buying a house while taking responsibility for its mortgage: the shares belong to investors, but the operating business must also support lenders. The EV-to-revenue multiple therefore values the whole business, not merely the stock.

Finally, J&J’s 3.3% free-cash-flow yield is not all available for dividends. Debt repayment, acquisitions, research, and legal settlements compete for that cash. The proposed $5.5 billion talc resolution could require as much as $3 billion in 2027, so valuation must move from today’s measures to the company’s history.

blocks.heading: What has Johnson & Johnson guided for 2026?

paragraphs.text: Management raised its full-year 2026 adjusted earnings per share, or EPS, forecast to **$11.05–$11.15**. EPS means profit allocated to each share. It estimated reported sales at **$101,000–$101,400 million**.

Operational growth removes the effect of translating foreign sales into dollars. Adjusted operational growth also removes the net effect of acquisitions and disposals. J&J expects adjusted operational sales growth of **6.4%–6.8%**, below reported growth of **7.2%–7.6%**. Both measures still benefit from an extra fiscal week in 2026, which brings sales but also wages and other costs.

blocks.heading: Has Johnson & Johnson kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: J&J has also made promises that can be checked against events. Duato told shareholders in March 2023 that J&J was preparing to become a more focused company with two sectors; the Kenvue separation was completed that August. A July 2026 presentation identified the OTTAVA surgical robot as a milestone, and October results reported its authorization to enter the market. Delivery matters, but an approval is not yet proof that a project has earned its cost.

blocks.heading: What is Johnson & Johnson's last eight-quarter trend?

paragraphs.text: September 2026 revenue rose 5.9% year over year, while organic growth reached 6.1%. Gross margin fell from 69.6% to 68.1%, but that modest change cannot explain operating income collapsing from $7,511 million to $65 million.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in Johnson & Johnson's next results?

paragraphs.text: The conditional talc proposal is the largest near-term legal cash question. J&J committed **$5.5 billion**, subject to participation by **95.0%** of remaining claimants. The first payment is capped at **$3 billion in 2027**. Accounting can record the obligation before the instalments leave the bank, so reported earnings and cash flow may look worst in different periods.
